notes: Company background: mid-market UX/product tooling for B2B SaaS — 450 employees, global customers, heavy EU customer base.
Primary product: embeddable onboarding copilot that guides users through first-run flows with step-by-step prompts and action suggestions.
Why Redwood: they want predictable latency for in-app guidance (streaming) and fine-grained token spend controls to keep CAC/unit economics healthy.
POC ask: start on Hosted API for quick test, instrument latency traces, then move to Dedicated if we can hit 99th pct SLO + stable per-token cost estimate.
Latency target: 99th percentile end-to-end < 300ms for US, <400ms EU (includes network + model). Customer emphasized UI jitter kills adoption.
Token caps: must have per-session and per-user token caps; product team wants automatic truncation + cost alerting when sessions approach limits.
Streaming: must support streaming partial responses and mid-generation tool-calls (e.g., fetch user data, run internal rule engine). Concern: how to handle tool-call latency and fallback text.
Routing: would like policy to route to cheaper model variant when not in critical SLO (background suggestions), and fall back to high-SLA model for in-flow assistance.
Security: SSO for Redwood Console, audit logs for all API calls tied to workspace, optional KMS for encryption-in-use, need EU data residency for onboarding transcripts.
Cost sensitivity: finance wants an upper bound on monthly token spend for the POC; asking for simulation of token usage per new user cohort (we supplied sample calc sheet).
Quote from product lead Marta: "If response feels laggy, conversion drops instantly. We need streaming that feels instant even if model is heavy."
Technical note from SE: recommend prefix caching for onboarding flows (lots of repeated system + prompt scaffolding), configure batching threshold carefully to avoid added tail latency.
Competitive notes: they evaluated OpenAI for ease of use but worried about cost predictability; Anthropic tested for safety; Cohere for embeddings but not ideal for streaming tool calls.
Next steps on POC: instrument real user flows (3 templates), run 1k simulated sessions to validate 99th-pct latency and token distribution, adjust batching and cache settings.
Admin: procurement expects an SOW for Dedicated if POC passes; legal requested standard DPA + security appendix (we pushed Redwood template).
Sales strategy: propose Hosted POC with clear success criteria -> Dedicated reserved commit conversation at POC completion -> Optimize recommendations to lower unit cost.
